title: The Brain: A Broadcasting and Receiving Station for Thought
coreMove: Treat thought like a signal: charge it with definite emotion, repeat it through auto-suggestion, then give creative imagination quiet time to catch plans.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders weighing speculative language against useful practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep the scientific color without treating names as proof
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Bell and Gates as period anchors while preserving the practical hard edge

exampleSpecs.audience: teams with facts but little emotional force
exampleSpecs.stakes: turn a cold message into a signal people can act on
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the radio analogy stepping a message up for sending and down for reception

exampleSpecs.audience: people who confuse inspiration with a repeatable practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: link the three principles into one operating routine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: combine subconscious sending, creative imagination receiving, and auto-suggestion

exampleSpecs.audience: presenters whose message has facts but no current
exampleSpecs.stakes: raise intensity without confusing intensity for proof
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: emotion raises the intensity of thought while tests still matter

exampleSpecs.audience: people who wait for inspiration without a control method
exampleSpecs.stakes: put the mental station to work through repeated self-instruction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: auto-suggestion is the operating method for the mental station

exampleSpecs.audience: creative teams checking hunches against tests
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep the received idea while repairing the weak execution
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use stepping up and stepping down to separate signal from implementation
